zen.description: Control Firefox/Zen through its shared tab. Pass operation fields in args. Start with status or pair. Navigate: {op:'navigate',args:{url:'https://example.com'}}. Observe: {op:'snapshot',args:{max_chars:6000}}. Act: {op:'run',args:{steps:[{action:'click_ref',ref:'ax-1'}],snapshot:false}}. Get any operation's parameters with {op:'help',args:{op:'run'}}. Use run for dependent actions and extract for rows. Existing sharing, permissions, input mode and cancellation apply. Inspect after uncertain errors before retrying.

browse.name: execute
browse.description: Run JavaScript that drives the browser: the user's real Chrome-family browser, through the browse extension. The code is an async function body (a single expression is returned; `return` a value to get it back) running in a small sandboxed JavaScript engine on the relay: no Node, no require/import, no fs, process or fetch (fetch belongs to the page: use page.evaluate). Synchronous code stops after about 2 seconds without an await. The result has the returned value (JSON, or the string as is), console output, warnings, and what happened to the page (URL changes, navigations, handoffs, a bot challenge: hand interactive ones to the user with handoff(), never solve or retry-loop them). Return a screenshot (`return await page.screenshot()`) to see it. Tabs are the handle: without `tab`, `page.goto(url)` opens a new tab; the result starts with `tab: <id>`, which you pass as `tab` to the next execute to continue there (with the same `state`). Close tabs you opened when you're done (`page.close()`).

code.description:
JavaScript (an async function body). Globals:
- page: a Playwright-style Page for the tab passed as `tab`; without one it has no tab until its first goto(url), which opens a new tab. goto(url, {waitUntil, timeout}), url(), title(), content(), evaluate(fn | string, arg), $eval/$$eval, waitForTimeout/Selector/URL/LoadState/Function, click/fill/type/press/hover/selectOption/check/uncheck(selector, ...), locator(selector), getByRole/Text/Label/Placeholder/TestId/AltText/Title, frameLocator, keyboard.press/type, mouse.click/move/wheel, screenshot({path, fullPage}), goBack/goForward/reload, setViewportSize, close(). Locators: click, dblclick, fill, clear, type, pressSequentially, press, hover, check, uncheck, selectOption, setInputFiles, textContent, innerText, innerHTML, inputValue, getAttribute, isVisible/Hidden/Checked/Enabled/Disabled, count, all, first, last, nth, filter, locator, getBy*, waitFor, evaluate, evaluateAll, allTextContents, boundingBox, screenshot, dragTo. Selectors are CSS or Playwright selectors (role=button[name="Save"], text=Sign in, >> nth=0, iframe >> frame >> ...). Locators are strict: one element.
- context.newPage() (a new tab), context.pages() (the tabs this execute works in and their popups); browser.contexts().
- snapshot(options?) → a compact outline with refs (options: find, diff, delta, interactive, within, mode: "aria"); ref("e12") → a locator for a snapshot ref. Prefer snapshot + ref over guessing selectors.
- handoff(message, {timeoutMs?, start?}) when only the user can proceed (login, 2FA, captcha, payment); demonstrate(message) to watch the user do a flow.
- screenshotWithLabels(), screenshotDiff({baseline}), network.start/status/stop/cancel, pageConsole.start/read/stop, webmcp.list/call(name, input).
- browse.<tool>(args): any browse tool directly (navigate, snapshot, click, fill, type, press, select, hover, drag, scroll, eval, wait_for, dialog, upload, emulate, webmcp, screenshot, screenshot_diff, network, console, recording, tabs, handoff, demonstrate, status, settings); they act in `page`'s tab unless you pass `tab` (browse.navigate without one opens a tab for `page`); returns its JSON and throws its error.
- files.path(name), files.write(name, data), files.read(name, encoding?) inside the file roots (files.dir, files.roots).
- state: an object kept with the tab between execute calls that pass it as `tab` (JSON values only).
- console.log/warn/error (shown in the result), setTimeout/clearTimeout/setInterval/clearInterval.

timeoutMs.description: Overall timeout in milliseconds (paused while handoff waits on the user); default 60000, 0 for none. Includes waiting behind another execute in the same tab.

tab.description: The tab `page` stands for: the `tab` an earlier execute (or navigate, tabs) returned. Leave it out to start without a tab; page.goto(url) then opens one.

cost_note: Actual CLI usage is retained. Signed-in subscription does not provide per-trial dollar charges.
measurement: Fresh host conversation per run. Host elapsed includes startup, model turns, navigation, waits, failures and retries. Task elapsed additionally includes independent answer/evidence validation. Profile setup and neutral-tab reacquisition are separate. Verification is not cut off the timer. Browser output UTF-8 bytes and characters are separate from model input/output/cached tokens.
scope: 6 public informational workflows, 2 repetition(s), engines zen,browse. Anonymous owned browser profiles; initially the first round is cold per site and the second is warm. A resumed phase resets profiles and is explicitly identified in phase metadata. Fixed gold facts for stable pages; time-stamped official JSON/API oracles for mutable metadata. Native task-tool catalogs differ and are saved. Not a store-install, authenticated-account or production reliability test.
